exposure: relative expression of oxytocin receptor (OXTR) mRNA
outcome: canine dystocia (complete uterine inertia, partial uterine inertia, obstructive dystocia, medically treated dystocia)
cohort: The study included 58 bitches, categorized into groups with complete uterine inertia, partial uterine inertia, obstructive dystocia, elective cesarean section, medically treated dystocia, and normal parturition.
finding: Progesterone concentrations and OXTR mRNA expression were highest in elective CS, while PGFM was highest in normal parturition, supporting their roles in the etiology of canine dystocia.
mod_finding: Cesarean section groups (elective, complete uterine inertia, partial uterine inertia, obstructive dystocia) exhibited significant differences in progesterone, PGFM, progesterone:PGFM ratio, and OXTR mRNA expression compared to each other and to controls and medically treated dystocia groups.
cross-section timing: near term and in dystocia, prior to CS or medical treatment, and during CS for uterine samples
